title: Memory Management
description: Understand stack vs heap, manual memory allocation, and safe memory patterns. Learn when and how to use malloc/free.
objectives: Use malloc and free for dynamic memory
Avoid memory leaks and dangling pointers

sections.title: Stack vs Heap
sections.content:
BPL has two types of memory:

**Stack** (automatic)
- Local variables live here
- Automatically freed when scope ends
- Fast but limited size
- Can't outlive the function

**Heap** (manual)
- Allocated with `malloc`
- Must be freed with `free`
- Can be any size
- Lives until you free it

```bpl
frame example() {
    local x: int = 5;           # Stack
    local p: *int = malloc(4);  # Heap
    # ... use p ...
    free(p);                    # Must free!
}
```

sections.title: Memory Management Comparison
sections.explanation: BPL uses manual memory management like C. You must free what you allocate.

sections.title: Common Memory Errors
sections.content:
**Memory Leak** - Allocate but never free:
```bpl
local p: *int = malloc(4);
# Forgot to free!
```

**Double Free** - Free same memory twice:
```bpl
free(p);
free(p);  # CRASH!
```

**Use After Free** - Access freed memory:
```bpl
free(p);
*p = 10;  # UNDEFINED!
```

**Null Dereference** - Access null pointer:
```bpl
local p: *int = nullptr;
*p = 10;  # CRASH!
```

**Buffer Overflow** - Write past allocation:
```bpl
local arr: *int = malloc(5 * 4);  # 5 ints
*(arr + 10) = 99;  # OUT OF BOUNDS!
```

sections.title: Memory Safety Guidelines
sections.content:
✅ **Always check malloc return value**
```bpl
local p = malloc(size);
if (p == nullptr) { return error; }
```

✅ **Use defer for cleanup**
```bpl
local p = malloc(size);
defer { free(p); }
```

✅ **Set pointer to nullptr after free**
```bpl
free(p);
p = nullptr;  # Prevents use-after-free
```

✅ **One owner per allocation**
- Clear ownership: who allocates, who frees

✅ **Prefer stack when possible**
- Heap only for dynamic sizes or data that outlives scope

sections.title: Practice: Safe String Buffer
sections.instructions:
Create a `StringBuffer` struct with:
- `data: *char` - heap-allocated character array
- `len: int` - current length
- `cap: int` - capacity

Implement:
- `create(cap: int) ret StringBuffer`
- `destroy(this: *StringBuffer)`
- `append(this: *StringBuffer, c: char)` - add character

Use defer for cleanup.
sections.hint: Similar to IntVec, but with char instead of int.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **Stack** is automatic, **heap** is manual

✅ `malloc(size)` allocates, `free(ptr)` deallocates

✅ **Always check** if malloc succeeded

✅ Use **defer** for guaranteed cleanup

✅ **sizeof<T>()** gives size in bytes

✅ Avoid: leaks, double-free, use-after-free

✅ Wrap allocations in **structs with destroy methods**

questions.question: What happens if you call malloc and never call free?
questions.explanation: Memory leak - the memory is never returned to the system until program ends.

questions.question: What does defer do?
questions.explanation: defer schedules code to run when the current scope exits, perfect for cleanup.

questions.question: After free(p), what should you do with p?
questions.explanation: Setting p = nullptr prevents accidental use-after-free bugs.
